restrictions: Two distinct 135-byte messages M(t) = U || 0^40 || U || 0^15, U the 40 little-endian bytes of a 320-bit parameter t, so that with SHA3 padding (byte 135 = 0x86) each message is one absorbed block. t ranges over the cosets t_j + span(W40), j < 256 G, of the 40-dimensional field W40 listed in proof.md Section 3, with origins t_j drawn as fresh randomness (two independent uniform random 256-bit words per coset, Section 6.1) and the fixed Gray order of each coset; only the survivors, the messages whose digest bits z = 0 and z = 1 of lanes 0 to 3 are zero (Section 5.5), are probed, and the two output messages have equal digests.

Complete SHA3-256 sponge of sha3-256-r6-prefix-v1: zero initial state, rate 136 bytes, suffix 0x06 with pad10*1, rounds 0 to 5 of Keccak-f[1600] in the single permutation call, full 256-bit digest; an ordinary collision.

Classical 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5 with reference operation cost 1626: a six-round permutation is one unit, every other operation 1/1626 (none is made: verification evaluates the six rounds in 1108 word operations per message); generated straight-line code with immediate addresses (Section 5.1). Each list's batch kernel is generated at run time by a word-RAM program that counts its own operations; a generation is charged 10370000 + 147 (Section 5.7). N = 7128337109634742553212499969700732807596 word operations (Section 10): the setup (eight XOR-forms), the plane-major FES, the filter test (9 per point), the extraction, a batch kernel of at most 37950 instructions per 256 survivors, a generic kernel for at most one batch in 512, per-lane lists, 2436 (R + 2^100 + 255 L) for tag passes and 2^70 + 16; G = 19293989233187077583904692. time_log2 = 121.72165 is log2(N/1626) rounded up, by the integer certificate 1626^100000 2^12172164 <= N^100000 < 1626^100000 2^12172165.

Memory below 2^144 words, 2^149 bytes: a direct array of 2^140 words (the key words, in [2^143, 2^144)) that is never initialized (the value-masked table: every written word carries a fresh 128-bit tag above the identifier, so any initial memory is handled, Lemma 8), survivor slots in [2^127, 2^127 + 2^126) (fewer than 2^125 written), coset records, a work region below 2^36 words, and generated code below 2^62 words (Section 11.1). Preprocessing at most 2^70 + 16 word operations (below 2^59.34 target compressions), included in time_log2: code generation, the generic kernel and the generator's tables, constants, byte tables, the certificate and the search that produced W40 (Section 11.2). No advice.

Success at least 0.39 is a probability over the algorithm's fresh coins (the random coset origins, drawn by a leader step charged at 11 operations per coset and 5 per group, a 128-bit table tag and the 2^16 signature words of the kernel generator). It rests on one declared score-critical heuristic, H_coset: over those coins the occupancy, key-match and triple bounds of proof.md Section 9 hold for the processed survivors (Section 12), and on a supporting budget heuristic H_K (Section 12.5): given all earlier lists, a list's generated kernel is over budget with probability at most 2^-10, else the generic kernel runs and a halt stops the run above one batch in 512. Proved in proof.md: two-round affinity on every coset of W40, degree at most 8 before the last chi, exactness of the Gray-order differences, the filter word, the extraction, the value-masked table for any initial memory, the duplicate-coset bound, detection up to a bounded triple event, the signature term, and every operation count.

No full-scale run and no collision are claimed. Four declared experiments execute the reference schedule, which shares the setup, the table and the verification with the claimed algorithm (introduction of Section 5), at a reduced size through a counting machine that stops unless every executed count equals its formula; they also execute at that size the claimed algorithm's setup code, plane-major FES of the eight forms and filter word, checked against the survivors of the emitted keys, but not its extraction (Appendix D). fes-campaign-reduced checks for a full collision (none expected); hcoset-within16 and hcoset-cross16 test a reduced-width H_coset on the run's own digests, hcoset-filter8 the survivor count and survivor pair rate (Section 12.2). The fifth, hk-kernel, runs the kernel generator and the generated programs on 20 lists and tests H_K (Section 12.5). A mask success is not a collision; nothing about cost is inferred.

heuristics.statement: Score-critical. The coins of the hypotheses are the C = 256 G coset origins t_j (G = 19293989233187077583904692), independent and uniform on F_2^320, each drawn from two calls of the cost model's primitive 'independent uniform random 256-bit word' (proof.md Section 6.1). For the Q = 2^48 G messages they generate, with the fixed Gray enumeration of span(W40) inside each coset, let D be the event that the C cosets are distinct (Pr[not D] <= C(C, 2) 2^-280 < 6.3e-30, proved, Lemma 7); a survivor is a message whose digest bits z = 0 and z = 1 of lanes 0 to 3 are zero; P the processed survivors (those of the lists processed before the run stops; |P| <= S_cap = S + ceil(S/2^20), S = 2^40 G, by the halt), F1 the event that no two survivors of P share a digest, X the number of unordered pairs of survivors of P with equal 140-bit keys and Y the number of bad triples in P (Lemma 9). Assume, over the coins: (a) Pr[F1 | D] <= 1/T40 + 2^-100 with T40 = sum_{k<=40} lambda^k/k! and lambda = Q(Q - 1)/2^265; (b) E[X | D] <= S_cap(S_cap - 1)/2^133 and Var[X | D] <= S_cap(S_cap - 1)/2^133; (c) E[Y | D] <= S_cap(S_cap - 1)(S_cap - 2)/2^381; (d) each of the 2^18 G lists receives fewer than 2^24 survivors with probability at least 1 - 2^-300. These are the values that independent uniform digests of distinct messages give. No premise on the mean or variance of the survivor count is used: the halt is not a failure event (proof.md Section 9). Then the failure probability over the fresh coins (these origins, the table tag and the generator's 2^16 signature words) is at most the ten terms of proof.md Section 9 (the ninth, 2^-100, covers the halt of the generic kernel under the supporting heuristic H_K, the tenth, 1.876043e-37, the identification of two different sums by the signature words; among them Chebyshev at the verification cap R = r + ceil(sqrt(kappa r)), kappa = 19345871228983, r = ceil(S_cap(S_cap - 1)/2^133)) < 61/100 (exact rational comparison; G is the least group count for which it holds at this kappa), so the success probability is greater than 0.3900000000000000000000000058 (proof.md Section 9).
heuristics.scope: The randomized campaign at full size: C = 256 G independent uniform coset origins drawn by the algorithm, complete 40-dimensional cosets of span(W40) in the fixed Gray order, the full 256-bit digest, its eight-bit survivor filter and the 140-bit key projection of the survivors, conditioned on distinct cosets. The success probability is over these fresh coins for the fixed target. Nothing else in the claim bears on the success except the supporting budget heuristic H_K (Section 12.5, a term 2^-100 of the failure bound); nothing else is heuristic: two-round affinity, the degree bound, the exactness of the enumeration, the filter word, the extraction, the value-masked table, the duplicate-coset bound and every operation count are proved or executed in proof.md Sections 3 to 7, 9 and 10 and Appendices C and D.
heuristics.extrapolation: Evidence on the six-round target. (1) Organizer-executed at every run of the declared experiments hcoset-within16, hcoset-cross16 and hcoset-filter8 (proof.md Sections 12.2 and 13): on 2^17 digests of 256 cosets whose origins come from the organizer's trial seeds, the pair counts inside one coset at 16 bits and across cosets at 16 and 24 bits must lie within 4 standard deviations of their exact uniform expectations (511, 130560, 510), the number of survivors (digest bits 0 and 1 of lanes 0 to 3 all zero) in [422, 602] and the number of survivor pairs agreeing on 8 further bits within 4 sd of C(n, 2)/256, or the run fails; the organizer recomputes every returned 16-bit agreeing pair. (2) GPU, preregistered, our runs, on unfiltered digests (proof.md Section 12.1 and Appendix A, with the GPU-versus-organizer digest checks kept as a printout in A.6): batch W, 2^34 digests per run with uniform random coset origins in one 34-dimensional coset or 1024 cosets of dimension 24, exact equal-pair counts of 36- to 64-bit projections, 96 six-round field counts with z from -3.14 to +2.16, PASS; batches 1 to 3, 17 runs of 2^30 digests, 32-bit within-coset and 44-bit global projections, every count within 2.1 sigma. (3) GPU, our runs, not preregistered, on survivors (proof.md Section 12.4 and Appendix E): seven runs of 2^34 messages (65,536 random cosets, their first 2^18 Gray points or random positions, six and 24 rounds), about 2^26 survivors each, survivor counts within 1.31 sigma of expectation, bit biases, pair-collision rates at 16, 24 and 32 bits (no |z| above 2.66 in the Gray-order runs), per-coset counts and Gray-order gaps consistent with uniform, one gap statistic at z = 3.32 not seen in its repeat. (4) Sensitivity (Section 12.3): if the pair-collision rate is (1 - eps) of uniform, 0.39 is restored at 0.00742, 0.03785, 0.07778 and 0.21285 extra log2 cost for eps = 0.01, 0.05, 0.10 and 0.25 (integer certificates). The extrapolation is from projections of at most 64 bits, 2^17 to 2^34 messages and sub-cosets (9 to 34 dimensions; the first 2^18 points of survivor cosets) to the full 256-bit digest, its 132 free key bits, Q messages and complete 40-dimensional cosets; the full collision event is the premise, not a measurement.
heuristics.limitations: An assumption: no proof is known, and image size or balance do not imply it (a balanced linear map can be injective on every translate of a campaign space). On each coset every digest bit has degree at most 16 in the 40 inner variables, a real structure that also governs the eight filter bits. The organizer-executed tests reach 16 and 24 bits and 2^17 digests (about 512 survivors) per run; the preregistered GPU evidence reaches 64-bit projections, 2^34 digests and 34-dimensional sub-cosets; the survivor runs reach about 2^26 survivors, 32-bit projections, the first 2^18 Gray points of 65,536 cosets and origins from a 64-bit mixer, and were not preregistered. No test reaches 256 bits, complete cosets or Q messages, none measures the key-match variance or the triple rate at 132 free key bits or list counts at 2^30-point scale, and no full collision is observed. The time bound is computed at the uniform pair rate; a shortfall eps needs the larger G of proof.md Section 12.3. Assumed, not measured: (a) to (d) at full width and full scale.

heuristics.statement: Supporting. A list is a coset origin t (drawn by the algorithm, uniform on F_2^320, independent across cosets) together with one of the 2^10 blocks of its coset. For a list the kernel generator of proof.md Section 5.7 (the word-RAM program GENSRC of experiments/fes_campaign.py, run under its own operation counter) produces a batch program of K instructions per batch (loop control included), or halts. A list is over budget if K > K_BUD = 37950, or the counter exceeds GEN_BUD = 10370000 (the generator halts), or a mask is outside its table of 205 masks, or a key row is constant, or the graph reaches 65536 nodes, or a register is dead. H_K (conditional form): given everything computed before its generator starts (earlier lists in processing order, earlier blocks of its coset included, their survivors and status, the counters, its own survivor count), a list is over budget with probability at most 2^-10. Then E[generic batches] <= 2^-10 B_cap for any adaptive selection, and they number at most ceil(B_cap / 512), B_cap = ceil((S_cap + 255 L) / 256), except with probability below 2^-100 (Azuma-Hoeffding, proof.md Section 9 (viii)); the algorithm stops with failure above that count, and the time bound charges every batch and generation at its budget (Section 10), so it holds for every run.
heuristics.scope: The distribution of (K, G) over uniform origins and uniform block indices, for the generator GENSRC as in experiments/fes_campaign.py; K and the counter value G are deterministic functions of the list. Nothing in the success bound other than the term (viii) uses H_K, and the cost bound does not depend on it.
heuristics.extrapolation: Evidence on the target (proof.md Section 12.5). (1) Organizer-executed at every run of the declared experiment hk-kernel: the generator and the generated programs run on 20 lists drawn from the organizer's trial seeds; every list within K_BUD and GEN_BUD; the generated program executed on 256 messages with every table word checked against the reference hash; the Pearson correlations of K and of the generation count with the survivor count (first 2^10 Gray points of each block) below 0.7 in absolute value, or the run fails. (2) Participant-run, preregistered (rule and criteria written before the runs): sample A, 2000 lists, gives the budgets (mean + 6 sd of K and of G); sample B, 6,000 independent lists run with the budgets as halts: 0 over budget (if the probability were 2^-10 or more, none in 6,000 has probability at most 0.0029); on the same lists the survivors among the first 2^20 Gray points of each block: Spearman rank correlations of K and of G with the count and chi-square tests of the events K > q90, G > q90 against terciles of the count, all within the preregistered limits (|rho| <= 0.0452, chi-square <= 13.82). The extrapolation is from 6,000 lists to a probability of 2^-10, from the survivors of a sub-block of 2^20 points to the 2^30 points of a list, and from independent origins to the conditional form.
heuristics.limitations: Not proved: K and G are outputs of a program on a function of the origin that is pseudorandom in appearance; the tail beyond the samples is not measured; the independence test detects only dependences of the size of its limits, on a sub-block, and not one that lives only in the extreme tail where no list is over budget; the organizer-run experiment has few lists and little power. The generator's operation count is its own counter, an upper bound of the executed count by construction. Assumed: the conditional 2^-10 bound given all earlier lists, earlier blocks of the same coset included; measured, on lists of independent origins, so the unconditional rate only: 0 of 6,000 (ours), 0 of 20 (organizer).
